positive: Many Samsung Fold owners say they are happy with their devices and welcome Apple into the foldable space, with some admitting they are impressed.
Several commenters note Samsung has offered foldables for years, and hope the added competition pushes it to improve.
Apple's pencil support is seen as a weak spot for Samsung, with some wanting stylus support and water resistance back and calling the Duo appealing.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's foldable arrives years after Samsung's and copies its ideas, so it doesn't feel like a true first-generation product.
Some criticize Samsung's foldables for durability and software problems, such as screens failing after about a year, slowdowns over time, and trade-offs in thinness and features.
Others question the new device's size, weight and price, calling it too small or heavy and too expensive.

positive: Many viewers are impressed that the crease is barely visible or not noticeable, and see the matte inner screen as a smart way to hide it.
The matte finish and overall look of the inner display are praised as attractive and a thoughtful touch.
negative: Many dislike the matte, nano-texture-style inner screen, saying it looks washed out, grainy or inaccurate in color and lacks a glossy OLED look.
Commenters see the matte finish as a way to hide the crease, and say Apple doesn't show off the hinge or crease.
Several worry the inner display is fragile, with concerns about scratches when left open and about durability of repeated folding.

positive: Many commenters say the open and close animation is smooth, clean and polished, and that the designers deserve recognition or a reward.
Several Samsung fans and Apple skeptics concede the animation is impressive, and some say it is the most appealing part of the phone.
The effect of the front panel looking see-through, and animations that follow the hinge angle, drew praise, with one noting the possibilities for app developers.
negative: Many commenters say the price is far too high, especially with everyday costs rising, and that it is higher still in several other countries.
Several mock the folding animation as the headline feature, saying it is underwhelming for a flagship after so many years of development.
Some worry about durability and repair costs, and say competitors like Samsung offer better value through discounts.

positive: Many commenters plan to swap a Pro model for the Duo, saying they are excited by a new form factor after years of similar phones.
Viewers value a larger screen that folds to a pocketable size, expecting to carry an iPad or laptop less often.
Several say the camera and other Pro-level compromises matter little for everyday use, and note the Duo was never pitched as a Pro.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo's price as too high, especially when it comes with trade-offs compared with a Pro or Pro Max.
Camera downgrades and the missing Face ID are the most common deal breakers, with several choosing the 18 Pro or Pro Max.
Some call the Duo unproven or not ready, and plan to wait for a later version or keep their current phone.

positive: Several left-handed commenters say they would adapt to the device and still want it, treating handedness as a minor concern.
Commenters like the button and toolbar placement. They say it suits tablet-style use, pocket access and one-handed screenshots, and they don't mind it for left-handed use.
Many viewers praise the size and half-folded shape, and see uses for reading, medical work, navigation and retro-style gaming.
negative: Left-handed users expect the design to suit them poorly, with several commenters saying the layout seems built only for right-handed people.
The phone's weight, width when folded and added case thickness are seen as making one-handed use awkward or uncomfortable.
Some note that the unfolded layout puts key elements, such as the text field, awkwardly near the hinge.

positive: Many commenters say they are ready to buy, drawn by a foldable that works as both phone and tablet, replacing an aging iPad mini.
Several accept trade-offs like no telephoto camera or Touch ID, saying the screen, software and polished fold animation matter more.
Some plan to add extra protection such as AppleCare or pick larger storage, while one points to a cheaper rival with stronger specs.
negative: Many commenters see the price, around the $2,000+ range and far higher for top storage, as unaffordable, with jokes about loans and financing.
The price is seen as too high for what is offered, such as a missing Pro-level camera and design they consider basic or not new.
Some doubt demand or practical value, citing durability worries, awkward half-folded use, and not wanting a costly device that encourages more phone time.

positive: Many commenters say they are eager to buy the Duo, with some planning to pre-order and others saying they have waited a long time for a foldable iPhone.
Several see it as the first genuinely interesting iPhone in years, praising its design, premium materials, polished open/close feel and the ability to multitask.
Some note that foldable features already existed on Android, but even Android users and sceptics say they admire it or are being won over.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo as too expensive and plan to wait for a later generation, expecting first-gen flaws and a lighter, improved design.
Commenters doubt Apple's innovation, saying it holds back features for next year, copies rivals, and has let its iPhone design go stale.
Some worry about the durability of a first-generation foldable screen, and others question whether a foldable is useful or just a gimmick.

positive: Many commenters say Apple's software and UI feel polished and fluid, and that this sets the device apart from rivals.
Several people say idea-sharing between tech companies benefits consumers, and that competitors tend to follow whatever Apple does.
Many longtime Apple users express strong excitement and plan to buy it, citing the design, build quality and trust in the brand.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is borrowing features Android makers, especially Samsung, have offered for years, such as foldables, and call it unoriginal.
Some say the criticism should extend to other companies that follow trends rather than standing apart, not just Apple.
Others focus on the high price, first-generation risk, missing features and App Store restrictions, and say they will wait for later models.
Many commenters say the price is too high, and import costs make it even worse in some countries, such as Turkey, Australia and Bolivia.
Storage upgrades are seen as costly, and the base capacity is considered small for the price. Some note it costs more than an iPad.
Some doubt the value and build: basic software like autocorrect still seems flawed, the device may be awkward to open, and an older used iPad looks like a better buy.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Data through 2026-10-05. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are moderately positive. Mid-size audiences are the happiest.

- Small: 37.1% of 62 videos with a baseline outperformed, with an average relative lift of 6.4 (79 videos total). Net sentiment is +15 (43.8% positive, 29.3% negative, n=850 comments).
- Mid: 18.4% outperformed (n=38), with a lift of 1.1. Net sentiment is +22 (47.6% positive, 25.8% negative, n=492).
- Large: none of 17 videos with a baseline outperformed, with a lift of 0.54 (20 videos total). Net sentiment is +10 (39.0% positive, 29.1% negative, n=223).

The large-channel group is small, so treat it cautiously. These are associations in a comment sample, not proof that channel size causes the differences.
examples.sql:
WITH v AS (
 SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer
 FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
 JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
 WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
lift AS (
 SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
 FROM v GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
 SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pos_share,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS neg_share,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment
 FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id
 WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
 GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side,
 s.pos_share, s.neg_share,
 CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group
ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions looks like the most reliable format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=15) with a 33% outperformer rate and a mean rel_lift of 1.42. Explainer/tips has the same 33% rate and the highest rel_lift (1.91), but that's only n=3, so treat it as a hint.

Comparison videos follow at a 20% outperformer rate and 1.33 rel_lift (n=5).

Upgrade advice (n=6), keynote recaps (n=4), meme shorts (n=2), durability tests (n=1) and "other" (n=2) had no outperformers. Their rel_lift runs from 0.10 to 0.80. Most of those samples are very small.

Caveat: these are associations from a small set of Duo videos, not proof that format causes performance.
examples.sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.rel_lift) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
Two high-lift videos draw the most negative reactions.

1. WSJ News, "I Tried Apple's First Folding iPhone. Here Are 3 Takeaways" (first impressions): lift is 14.06 (relative lift 2.4). Net sentiment is -35, with 18% positive and 53% negative (n=17).

2. Both Sides of the Tech, "Apple Might Not Make Another iPhone Duo..." (upgrade advice): lift is 29.77 (relative lift 5.1). Net sentiment is -27, with 27% positive and 55% negative (n=11).

Both videos clearly outperformed, yet commenters lean negative about the product. The Both Sides of the Tech video had the bigger lift but a slightly milder negative reaction.

Caveat: n is small for both (17 and 11 product-side comments), so treat these as directional only.
examples.sql: SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator_name, c.format, p.lift, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY c.video_id, c.title, cr.name, c.format, p.lift, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer HAVING COUNT(*)>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 2

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
The largest topics are Excitement and durability tests (n=297, 13% of comments), Praise for the review (n=268, 11.8%), Price and value (n=185, 8.1%) and the Samsung Fold comparison (n=177, 7.8%).

Excitement and durability tests also grew the most in raw volume, from 29 comments the prior week to 160 this week (+131). Price and value added 85 (22 to 107) and Samsung Fold added 72 (17 to 89).

By percentage growth, the fastest are:
- Folding animation praise: +533% (6 to 38)
- Productivity, keyboard and iPad: +500% (3 to 18)
- Excitement and durability tests: +452%
- Apple copying accusations: +444% (9 to 49)

Caveat: prior-week counts are small, so the percentages look dramatic. Productivity, keyboard and iPad is tiny (n=27 total), so treat its growth cautiously. No sentiment data was in this result.
examples.sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prior_week FROM sc, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sc),3) AS share_of_all_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prior_week, a.n_this_week-a.n_prior_week AS change_n, ROUND(CASE WHEN a.n_prior_week>0 THEN 1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prior_week)/a.n_prior_week END,3) AS growth_pct, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
examples.a:
Duo sits in the upper range, with a net sentiment of +20 (46% positive, 26% negative, n=1,418 comments across 129 videos). That is well above general event coverage (-9, n=86) and the "other" topic (-11, n=66), where negative comments outnumber positive ones.

Only competitor foldables score higher, at +30 (49% positive, 19% negative). That rests on just 43 comments from 3 videos, so treat it as a rough signal. iPhone 18 Pro is +8, but n=13 from 2 videos is too small to read anything into.

Caveat: these figures come from a sample of comments, so they describe the commenters, not all viewers. The non-Duo topics all have small samples, so the gaps between them are tentative.
examples.sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10' END AS n_check FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Commenters like the folding animation and the excitement and durability-test content most, and they criticise price and value most.

Liked: the folding animation has a net sentiment of +28 (53% positive, 25% negative, n=96). Excitement and durability tests score +27 (49% positive, 22% negative, n=297), and the Samsung Fold comparison scores +25 (52% positive, 27% negative, n=177).

Criticised: price and value is the heaviest target, at +14 net (48% positive, 34% negative, n=185). Accusations of Apple copying Android are next at +5 (36% positive, 31% negative, n=83, a small sample). The inner screen and crease also draws pushback, at +12 (n=155).

No topic is net negative, so criticism is more a matter of degree than a dominant theme. Topics are tallied separately and comments may overlap, so this is a sample of comments, not all viewers.
examples.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.comment_id, cm.sentiment, cm.topic_id FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL), t AS (SELECT tp.topic_id, tp.name, COUNT(*) AS n_comments, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM c JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE tp.pool='product' GROUP BY tp.topic_id, tp.name) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, n_comments, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n_comments,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n_comments,3) AS neg_share FROM t ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, n_comments, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n_comments,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n_comments,3) AS neg_share FROM t ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)
